text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- Several key conservative and liberal politicians are planning to leave the Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) in protest against the recent strengthening of nationalist and Catholic hard-liners, the newspaper learned from a source who declined to be named.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Former communist countries which will soon start negotiating an NATO entry will not have to carry out costly military equipment upgrading and infrastructure modernisation programmes, NATO's Military Committee chairman Klaus Naumann said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The Polish Banking Association has demanded that the National Bank of Poland (NBP) and the finance ministry change banking regulations which force Polish banks to show obligatory reserve and credit concentration rates.
The regulations blunt the local banks' competitive edge in comparison to foreign banks.
- The last issue of ailing Catholic daily Slowo-Dziennik Katolicki will appear on April 30, as its planned takeover by a church foundation headed by Father Tadeusz Rydzyk did not take place.
- Poland will not face certain problems now troubling the Czech Republic as Polish macroeconomic reforms coincided with changes on the corporate level, Finance Minister Marek Belka said.

- Regional investment funds will be formed in order to accelerate the privatisation and restructuring of companies operating within regional development programmes supported by the government, Polish Investment Bank (PBI) official Marcin Grabiennik said.

- The Stocznia Gdynia shipyard has launched a 30,600 dead-weight tonnage (DWT) container ship contracted by Germany's KG Projex of Hamburg and an 18,400 DWT container vessel contracted by Germany's Alpha Ship.
- Finland's Neste petrochemical concern this year will invest $1.5 million in construction of a polyester resin plant in Gdansk province, northern Poland.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- U.S.-based Intel Corporation computer processor maker is planning to extend cooperation with Poland's Optimus and JTT computer makers, Intel's deputy president Craig Barret said.
- Holland's Philips concern will move production to Poland and eastern European countries for low labour costs and proximity to western markets, Philips' deputy president Dudley Eustace said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The bankrupt Gdansk shipyard will be contracted to carry out construction of three ships for Germany's Schoeller Holdings Ltd when Polsat television president and co-owner Zygmunt Solorz signs a letter of intent later this week, the yard's receiver Andrzej Wiercinski said.
- Britain's Uren Coldstores has bought the Krespol fruit freezing plant in Laszczow worth 2.83 million zlotys.
- The US. Foster Wheeler boiler maker will install two boilers at the Jaworzno 3 power plant worth $60 million in two years time.
ZYCIE
- The gross balance sheet total of Poland's banking sector was 207.6 billion zlotys in 1996, the banks' reports showed.
PARKIET
- The Browar Szczecin brewery is planning to increase share capital to 14.5 million zlotys through an issue of 600,000 shares priced at 10 zlotys each.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
